summary: Gobbler Knob in Grays Harbor County had a 1940s camp, then an 8x8 cab on a trailer from 1960 that was gone by 1966; Willhite found no sign of it on the summit.

facts.design: 8 by 8 foot cab on a trailer, built 1960; a camp preceded it in the 1940s
facts.status_note: Cab and trailer gone by 1966; Willhite found no evidence of a lookout on the summit when he visited

staffing.status: Gladys Bertrand named as lookout for 1962 and 1963 (Willhite); a 1964 newspaper item says the site was to be manned that June

access.note: Quinault Tribe land; Willhite says permission is now required

visit.trail_note: Per Willhite: gravel roads off Highway 101, a walk of 1/2 mile or less with about 150 feet of gain; permission required

8x8 foot cab and trailer built on the site

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Willhite places 1963 as the last year; a 1964 newspaper item quoted on the Washington lookout list says Gobbler Knob was to be manned in June 1964. Both are reported in the story and the story does not pick one.
Willhite says a logging date of about 1959 might match when a trailer went on top, but the register and firelookout.com both give 1960. The story uses 1960.

sources.title: Gobbler Knob Lookout Site - Olympic Mountains

notes_for_editor: This is the Grays Harbor site (us-wa-gobbler-knob). It is not the Mount Rainier Gobblers Knob (us-wa-gobblers-knob), which already has its own story and research; the names are near-identical, so keep them apart. The last staffed year is disputed (1963 per Willhite, 1964 per a newspaper item quoted on the weebly list; that item says the site was to be manned, not that it was). The weebly page is a statewide list and only its Gobbler Knob entry was used. Willhite's visit date is not given. Willhite's photo captions (1958 to 1972) are not used because they do not say what stands on the site. The brief's access 'unknown' is replaced with permission, per Willhite.
